oleō

oleō, olēre, oluī

verb, second conjugation

smell, smell of

In this lexicon

  • smell

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 2.1.1: bene olēre; Ter. Ad. 1.2.37: olet unguenta (Lewis & Short); Traupman 381

Examples

  • et, ut mulierēs, ideō bene olēre quia nihil olēbant vidēbantur.

    and, like women, they seemed to smell good precisely because they smelled of nothing.Cic. Att. 2.1.1

    In the entry for smell

  • Postume, nōn bene olet quī bene semper olet.

    Postumus, a man who always smells good doesn’t smell good.Mart. 2.12.4

    whenever you’ve eaten threads of strong-smelling Tarentine leek, kiss with your mouth shut.Mart. 13.18.1–2
